brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A flat, longjing-style green tea from the banks of the Meijiang river in Meitan, Guizhou province, also known as Meijiang Cuipian.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It was first made in 1943, during the war against Japan, at an agricultural research tea station in Meitan, which copied longjing methods using the local Meitan Taicha population. The name was fixed in 1954. It was rated a quality product of Guizhou from 1986 to 1992 and received a ministry award in 1988.
processing: Withering of the picked shoots, then pan-firing by hand in five stages: kill-green, cooling, second firing, cooling again and a final low-heat firing, with ten hand motions adapted to the leaf.
harvest_season: Picked around Qingming, with pre-Qingming leaf rated best; top grades take one bud with an opening leaf.
appearance_dry: Flat, smooth and straight, shaped like sunflower seeds, bright green with sparse down.
appearance_wet: Tender, even green buds and leaves that open in the cup.
taste_profile: Clean aroma of chestnut with fresh floral notes; mellow, brisk and sweet in the finish.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
